Hi Priyom,

Thanks for the quick intro last week. Our security team reviewed Redwood's public materials and ran a quick gap analysis against our vendor baseline. A couple of specific clarifications we need before we can move to legal/procurement:

- How does Redwood classify incoming customer data that contains PII? Do you support automated classification + human review, or is classification expected to be done by the customer?
- For cross-border transfers, what mechanism do you use (SCCs, BCRs, other)? If SCCs, can you confirm which version and whether you accept our annex?
- Do you offer pseudonymization at ingestion or only at rest? If at ingestion, is this reversible and who holds the key?
- Key custody: can customers bring their own keys (BYOK/HSM) for encryption-at-rest, or is it Redwood-managed KMS only?
- What is your default audit/log retention for access logs (console/API/token usage)?

I've attached our short security questionnaire (Novamed_Security_Questionnaire.xlsx) and highlighted the PII/dataflow sections. If you can return high-level answers and any supporting artifacts (high-level dataflow PNG, KMS attestation template, draft transfer annex), that will keep procurement moving.

Appreciate it — Elena
Senior Information Security Manager
Novamed Health

Hi Elena —

Thanks for the questionnaire and the clear asks. High-level answers below; attaching a concise dataflow diagram and a short note on our pseudonymization options. Happy to expand any section.

1) PII classification: Redwood provides an optional automated classification layer (regex and ML heuristics) for common PII types (SSNs, emails, phone numbers). Customers can enable classification at ingestion; however we treat classification results as advisory. Final classification and retention policy are controlled by the customer. We can provide exportable classification logs for audits.

2) Cross-border transfers: For hosted customers we rely on standard contractual mechanisms. We support SCCs (EU Commission 2021 modules) and, where requested under enterprise contracts, we can negotiate a transfer annex. We do not currently operate on BCRs.

3) Pseudonymization: We support two patterns: (a) reversible tokenization (customer-managed keys recommended) and (b) one-way hashing for non-reversible pseudonymization. Reversible tokenization uses envelope encryption: data encrypted with a data key, which is itself wrapped by the KMS key. Key access controls determine reversibility.

4) Key custody: Customers may choose Redwood-managed KMS (default) or BYOK using supported cloud HSMs (AWS KMS with imported key material, Google Cloud External Key Manager, or an on-prem HSM in Private deployments). When BYOK is used, Redwood never has unwrapped access to the keys.

5) Audit/log retention: Default audit logs are retained for 90 days in the Console. We offer extended retention add-ons (1 year / 3 years) as part of enterprise packages; for evidence requests we can export immutable log slices and provide a signed timeline.

Attachments: redwood_dataflow_v2.png; redwood_pseudonymization_notes.txt

Next steps: please flag which artifacts you need in final form (e.g., signed transfer annex, KMS attestation). If useful, we can set up a 30-min technical call Thursday to walk through the dataflow and keystore options.

Cheers,
Priyom Das

Hi Elena — looping in legal/product for the transfer/attestation items. A few concrete confirmations and attachments below.

- Transfer mechanism: Redwood is prepared to execute the EU SCCs (2021) with a supplemental transfer annex. I've attached a draft transfer annex (dpa_transfer_annex_draft.pdf) that includes the Novamed-specific clause placeholders. We can accept most reasonable edits; please mark up and we'll triage with legal.

- KMS attestation: attached is a template (kms_attestation_template.docx) we can populate. Key custody options: 
  * Customer-managed (BYOK): supported in hosted + private (recommended for high-sensitivity customers). When enabled, Redwood stores only wrapped keys; unwrapping requires customer-side control.
  * Redwood-managed: keys are held in the cloud provider KMS under encryption policies. We provide audit logs for KMS operations and can produce signed statements for rotations/rotations policy.

- Log retention: default 90 days; we can provide contractual 12-month retention with archive exports for enterprise customers (this requires a retention add-on and may affect cost). We will provide immutable, timestamped exports (WORM-style) on request for audits.

- Subprocessors: Our current subprocessors list is maintained on the privacy portal. For transparency, CloudEast is not listed as a subprocessor at this time for hosted services; the primary cloud infra subcontractors are CloudMajor (compute) and BlobStoreCo (object storage). If you have a specific integration that references CloudEast, send the artifact and we'll trace it. We will also include the subprocessor CSV extract in the next message if helpful.

Attachments: dpa_transfer_annex_draft.pdf; kms_attestation_template.docx
